$comment: Expert rules, applied by engine/solve in file order after priors, vocabulary and instrument corrections; each firing rule id is appended to the rule trace. condition atoms: {param, gt|gte|lt|lte}, {archetype: [...]}, {instrument: [...]}, {instrumentKind: [...]}, {pickup: [...]}, {descriptor: [...]}, {enabled: block}, {disabled: block}, {modelPrefix: {block: prefix}}; combinators {all: [...]}, {any: [...]}, {not: cond}. A param atom is false when the block is disabled or its model lacks the param. action is a list of {set|add|min|max: {param: value}}, {enable|disable: [block]}, {warn: text}. min/max are floors/caps. Params use canonical '<block>.<param>' keys (vocabulary.paramAliases).

rules.rationale: Jazz clean tones rely on the amp's clean headroom; a drive pedal adds grit that masks chord voicings.
Above ~40% most clean models start to break up; clean archetypes keep headroom.
Noise rises with gain; at high gain a gate is needed to keep pauses silent.
Single coils hum; under high gain the hum is amplified, so the gate threshold goes higher than for humbuckers.
rules.notes: Mighty Space's gate has Sensitivity (no Threshold); higher sensitivity is the threshold-up equivalent.

rules.rationale: Single-coil and P-90 hum becomes audible from crunch gain upward.
The mandolin's stacked humbucker is quiet and its notes decay fast; a strong gate chops the tail.
Pre-distortion bass is compressed into mud at high gain; keep amp bass at or below 60 and get weight from the cab.
A ~90 Hz low cut tightens palm mutes and leaves room for the bass guitar.
Fully scooped high-gain tones disappear in a band mix; keep some mids for cut.
High gain plus high treble produces fizz; a ~13 kHz high cut removes it without dulling the attack.
Delay and reverb together smear note definition; pull the reverb back so the repeats stay clear.
Reverb tails on saturated tones turn into noise; keep the mix low.
Lead delay should sit behind the dry note, not compete with it.

action.warn: Acoustic pickup into an electric amp model: expect quack and feedback. Try an acoustic prompt for amp-off + IR.

rules.rationale: Electric amp models are voiced for magnetic pickups; piezo/acoustic signals sound harsh through them.

action.warn: Acoustic sim with an electric guitar works best on the neck pickup with the tone rolled back.

rules.rationale: Acoustic body IRs exaggerate the bridge pickup's bite.

action.warn: This patch uses a User IR slot; load an acoustic IR there with Mighty Editor or it will sound wrong.

rules.rationale: User IR slots are empty or user-specific; the QR stores only the slot number.
Mandolin has no fundamental below ~196 Hz; a ~100 Hz low cut removes body boom and handling noise.
Boosting amp bass on mandolin adds boom and feedback, not warmth; warmth comes from lower treble.
Guitar humbucker advice (cut treble to tame bite) is the wrong direction for the mandolin's dark stacked humbucker; it needs treble to keep chop and tremolo picking clear.
Piezo pickups are boomy and feedback-prone below ~90 Hz.
